messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.reasoning:
The user says: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6."

They want the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test? That might refer to the standard error of the mean under null? Usually standard error = sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). But they mention "standard deviation of the null hypothesis test" maybe they want the standard error of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under null. That would be sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size) = 1.4 / sqrt(40). sqrt(40) ≈ 6.3249. So 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2213. So standard error ~0.221.

But maybe they want the standard deviation of the test statistic? For a t-test, the test statistic t = (sample_mean - population_mean) / (sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size)). The denominator is the standard error. So the standard deviation of the test statistic under null is sqrt(sample_size-1)/(sqrt(sample_size-1))? Actually t distribution has variance n-1/(n-3) for df>2. But maybe they want the standard error.

Given the phrasing, likely they want the standard error. So answer: 0.221.

We can compute precisely: 1.4 / sqrt(40) = 1.4 / 6.3249 = 0.2213.

Thus standard deviation of null hypothesis test = 0.2213.

We can also mention that this is the standard error of the mean. Provide the calculation.
